subject.title: Telegram forum: no reliable topic-name -> topic_id resolution for agent routing

question: Should OpenClaw expose a Telegram forum topic title-to-topic_id routing surface, and should it be prompt context, a `message` action, or a channel metadata/SDK endpoint?
rationale: Current main intentionally exposes topic names only after a numeric thread id is observed; choosing forward routing needs maintainer intent for duplicate titles, cache freshness, Bot API limits, and the contract agents/plugins can rely on.

options.title: Expose Observed Topic Catalog
options.body: Add a Telegram-owned list/catalog action or metadata endpoint that returns known topic ids, names, closed state, and freshness so agents can choose or ask when ambiguous.

options.title: Add Resolver-Only Helper
options.body: Add a direct name-to-id helper, returning structured ambiguity or stale-data errors instead of silently routing when names collide or cache data is old.

options.title: Keep Numeric-Only Routing
options.body: Leave topic names as display/context metadata and document numeric topic ids or `chatId:topic:<threadId>` as the only supported routing contract.

recommendation.title: Expose Observed Topic Catalog
recommendation.body: Add a Telegram-owned list/catalog action or metadata endpoint that returns known topic ids, names, closed state, and freshness so agents can choose or ask when ambiguous.

likelyOwner.reason: They are tied to merged topic-cache refinement and adjacent Telegram action surface history, which would likely anchor the resolver contract.
